claims.text: Equimolar WTaTiVZr has improved plastic strain and toughness relative to pure tungsten.
The high-entropy effect governs the improved plastic strain and toughness of WTaTiVZr.
Combining multiple principal elements produces a nanoscale landscape of local lattice distortions in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr may contain nano-precipitates generated by its multicomponent constitution.
The nanoscale heterogeneities impede dislocation channeling and dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion produces more homogeneous plastic flow during high-temperature deformation.
The nanoscale heterogeneities increase the strain-hardening rate.
The nanoscale heterogeneities delay the onset of plastic flow and yielding.
More uniform deformation improves resistance to fracture.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will exhibit a higher strain-hardening rate at 1200–1600 °C.
Relative to pure tungsten, WTaTiVZr will exhibit greater fracture toughness and total plastic strain capacity at 1200–1600 °C.
The predicted mechanical improvements will coincide with observable nanoscale heterogeneities and altered dislocation behavior.
The hypothesized nanoscale features remain stable up to approximately 1600 °C unless coarsening or phase transformations occur.
Thermal or irradiation-induced coarsening and phase transformations delimit the regime in which the proposed mechanism applies.
Processing variations may influence the microstructural evolution and mechanical response.

Pure tungsten is relevant as a plasma-facing-material benchmark because it has favorable high-temperature, thermal, sputtering, creep, tritium-retention, and irradiation-related characteristics, although it also has important embrittlement and oxidation limitations.
